intro: I am a Ph.D. student in Computer Science at Kennesaw State University, working in the Sustainable Smart Systems Lab (S³ Lab) with my advisor, Bobin Deng. Before the Ph.D. I spent eight years at BJIT Ltd., moving from Software Engineer to Principal Software Engineer, building secure microservices, retrieval-augmented knowledge tools, and enterprise PLM integrations.
bio_short: Priyabrota Sen is a doctoral researcher in Computer Science at Kennesaw State University, working on computer vision, video world models, and the evaluation of learned systems under real operating conditions. Current work spans a vision-driven digital twin for robotic production lines, a benchmark for learned noise adaptation in quantum error-correction streams, and difficulty-ranked masking for video world models. Before starting the Ph.D. in 2025, Sen spent eight years at BJIT Ltd., rising from Software Engineer to Principal Software Engineer and delivering secure Java/Spring Boot services, retrieval-augmented knowledge tools, and Dassault Systèmes ENOVIA PLM/PDM integrations.
bio_long: I am a doctoral researcher in Computer Science at Kennesaw State University, in the Sustainable Smart Systems Lab (S³ Lab) advised by Bobin Deng, where I work on computer vision and machine learning for systems that operate in the physical world. My current research follows three threads: a closed-loop digital twin in which a fine-tuned detector and multi-camera tracking drive a six-axis robot arm on a production-line testbed; video world models that decide what to mask during training by ranking objects by how hard they are to predict; and a large benchmark that treats quantum error-correction measurements as sparse binary video.

A common concern runs through all three: careful evaluation. I build datasets and benchmarks with held-out and calibration splits, compare models against tuned statistical baselines over multiple seeds, test differences for significance, and report where a learned method loses as well as where it wins. Several collaborations extend this to conformal prediction and calibrated decision-making in medical and surgical video.

I came to research after eight years in industry. At BJIT Ltd. in Bangladesh I was promoted twice, from Software Engineer to Senior and then Principal Software Engineer, and was named Best Senior Engineer of the Year in 2022. I built Java/Spring Boot microservices secured with OAuth2/JWT and HashiCorp Vault, a retrieval-augmented generation tool over enterprise PDF documentation, and integrations and data migrations for Dassault Systèmes ENOVIA / 3DEXPERIENCE PLM and PDM platforms.

That background shapes how I work now. I care about whether a model still performs after it is deployed, which is why my research reports latency on live camera streams, end-to-end task success on real hardware, and stage-by-stage error analysis alongside benchmark accuracy.

I hold a B.Sc. in Computer Science and Engineering from Khulna University of Engineering & Technology (KUET), where my thesis on error-correcting codes for memory reliability led to an IEEE conference paper.
